news.headline: Apple is Now the Top-Performing Magnificent 7 Stock in 2026. Here’s why it’s Beating NVIDIA, Tesla, and Amazon
news.summary: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) has emerged as the best-performing Magnificent Seven stock of 2026, outperforming NVIDIA (NVDA), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta Platforms (META), and Tesla (TSLA). But what's driving Apple's surprising rally while other AI stocks struggle? In this episode, 24/7 Wall St.'s Eric Bleeker examines why Apple shares have surged more than 27% in 2026, even as concerns about artificial intelligence spending are weighing on some of the market's biggest technology companies. While competitors are committing hundreds of billions of dollars to AI data centers, Apple is taking a different approach. Its strategy emphasizes on-device artificial intelligence, privacy, and integrating AI directly into its ecosystem, avoiding much of the enormous infrastructure spending burden facing its rivals. Eric breaks down Apple's latest earnings, its massive share repurchase program, and why investors are increasingly rewarding the company's capital-efficient AI strategy. He also compares the Magnificent Seven's performance in 2026 against their remarkable returns since the beginning of 2023, revealing a very different picture of the AI investment boom. Has Apple become the market's ultimate AI safe-haven stock? And could its strategy continue outperforming NVIDIA and the rest of Big Tech?

news.headline: The Next Stock Market Crash Could Start With Just 3 Companies
news.summary: Just three companies now account for approximately 21% of the S&P 500's total market capitalization. NVIDIA (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), and Microsoft (MSFT) have become so dominant that their performance could determine the direction of the entire stock market. But what happens if these technology giants stumble? In this episode, 24/7 Wall St. co-founder Doug McIntyre and senior writer Lee Jackson discuss the extraordinary concentration of the S&P 500 and why millions of investors may be taking on more risk than they realize. Much of today's market enthusiasm is driven by artificial intelligence. Companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta Platforms (META) have benefited from enormous expectations for AI growth. But Doug and Lee identify several potential threats to that optimism. They explore how cheaper open-source AI models could challenge industry leaders, why opposition to AI data center construction threatens expansion plans, and how growing electricity demand is driving renewed interest in nuclear power. Most importantly, they discuss what could happen to popular index funds like the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) if the market's largest technology stocks suffer a major sell-off. They also examine whether equal-weight S&P 500 funds could provide investors with better diversification. Is your S&P 500 investment more vulnerable than you think?
